resources.string: Tap to snooze all notifications until you turn it off again.
New notifications are quietly put aside. They come back as soon as you unsnooze.
Grant notification access to start snoozing.
Snoozer can\'t snooze anything until you allow it. Tap to see how.
Briefly show which app\'s notification was snoozed
Turn on a mode while snoozing
Adds a mode under Settings › Modes
Needs Do Not Disturb access. Tap to allow.

%1$s adds a mode called “%2$s” under Settings › Modes and turns it on while snoozing. Choose what it does in the mode settings, for example dim the wallpaper, use dark theme or decide who can still reach you. It can be combined with your other modes. Turning this off removes the mode again.
Snoozes when Bedtime mode starts and unsnoozes when it ends
Repeat this after reinstalling Snoozer. Updates keep the permissions.
Setup needed: follow the steps under One-time setup.
Can\'t read the Bedtime status on this phone.
Experimental: only tested on Pixel phones and may change in future versions.
On your phone, open Settings › About phone and tap Build number seven times to turn on Developer options.
Open Settings › System › Developer options and switch on USB debugging.
Connect your phone to a computer that has Android\'s platform tools (adb) and allow USB debugging when your phone asks.
Tap Copy commands, send the commands to the computer, and run them there in a command window.
Come back here and tap Check now.
%1$s has no schedules or triggers of its own, so it needs no background service. Tasker handles those much better.
A silent notification with an Unsnooze button while snoozing
Notifications are off for Snoozer. Tap to allow.
Shows that notifications are being snoozed
New notifications are put aside until you unsnooze.
Android only lets apps with notification access snooze notifications from other apps. Without it, Snoozer can\'t do its job.
Find %1$s in the list and switch on \"Allow notification access\".
Confirm by tapping \"Allow\" in the dialog.
Come back here. The snooze button is now ready to use.
Notification access is on. You can now snooze all notifications with one tap.
If you installed Snoozer from outside an app store, Android blocks this setting at first. Open App info, tap the ⋮ menu in the top corner, choose \"Allow restricted settings\", and try again.
Snoozer only uses this access to snooze and restore notifications. It never reads, stores or shares their content, and it has no internet access.
Snooze or unsnooze without opening the app: from Quick Settings, your home screen or a gesture.
Your phone can add the tile for you. Tap the button and confirm.
Tile added. Swipe down to find it.
The tile is already in your Quick Settings.
Your phone couldn\'t add the tile automatically. Please follow the steps below.
Swipe down twice from the top of the screen to open Quick Settings.
Tap the button to edit your tiles.
Find the \"%1$s\" tile and drag it to your active tiles.
Tap the tile to switch snoozing on or off. Touch and hold it to open Snoozer.
Touch and hold the %1$s app icon.
Tap \"%1$s\" to switch snoozing on or off instantly.
Optional: drag the shortcut onto your home screen for one-tap access.
Gesture: tap the back of your phone
Open Settings › System › Gestures › Quick Tap to start actions.
Turn on Quick Tap and choose Open app.
Tap the settings icon next to %1$s and pick the \"%2$s\" shortcut.
Double-tap the back of your phone to snooze or unsnooze.
On other phones, look for a back-tap or gesture feature that can open an app shortcut, such as RegiStar in Samsung\'s Good Lock.
%1$s is a Tasker plug-in. Let Tasker snooze your notifications automatically, for example at bedtime, during meetings or while driving.
In Tasker, open the Tasks tab and tap + to create a task.
Tap + to add an action, then choose Plugin › %1$s.
Tap the edit button next to Configuration, pick Snooze, Unsnooze or Toggle, and tap Save.
Go back to save the action. Run the task, or use it in a profile.
Snoozer also works in MacroDroid, Automate and any other app that supports Tasker/Locale plug-ins.
Choose what this action does when the task runs.
Stop snoozing and bring all notifications back
Switch between snoozing and not snoozing
Use colors from your wallpaper instead of the app’s blue
